You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To prepare your garden for winter, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Drain and coil the garden hoses (20 minutes)
Step 2. Inspect the perimeter for structural damage (1 hour)
Step 3. Apply a thick layer of insulating straw to strawberry beds (2 hours)
Step 4. Lock the garden shed for the season (5 minutes)
Step 5. Prune the climbing roses (45 minutes)
Step 6. Sharpen the blades on the loppers and shears (30 minutes)
Step 7. Research local frost dates and winter hardiness zones (1 hour)
Step 8. Spray dormant oil on fruit trees to prevent pests (1 hour)
Step 9. Dig up tender dahlia tubers (2 hours)
Step 10. Clean the mud off all hand shovels and rakes (40 minutes)
Step 11. Test the soil pH levels (30 minutes)
Step 12. Purchase organic soil amendments (45 minutes)
Step 13. Empty the fuel from the lawnmower (15 minutes)
Step 14. Rub linseed oil on wooden tool handles (20 minutes)
Step 15. Identify which perennial shrubs need heavy pruning (30 minutes)
Step 16. Cut back the herbaceous perennials to the ground (3 hours)
Step 17. Label the stored tubers with masking tape (15 minutes)
Step 18. Shake off excess soil from the harvested roots (30 minutes)
Step 19. Inventory the remaining garden twine and stakes (15 minutes)
Step 20. Store all hand tools in a dry, rust-proof bin (20 minutes)
Step 21. Gather all scattered plastic nursery pots (30 minutes)
Step 22. Clean the lawnmower deck of grass clippings (30 minutes)
Step 23. Rake the fallen maple leaves into piles (2 hours)
Step 24. Hang the tools on the wall rack (15 minutes)
Step 25. Collect seeds from dried flower heads (1 hour)
Step 26. Wipe down the potting bench (20 minutes)
Step 27. Spread a layer of finished compost over the vegetable beds (3 hours)
Step 28. Mix bone meal into the soil (1 hour)
Step 29. Turn the compost pile one last time (45 minutes)
Step 30. Organize the seed starting trays for next year (40 minutes)
Step 31. Order new burlap rolls for wrapping evergreens (20 minutes)
Step 32. Wrap the trunks of young trees to prevent sunscald (1 hour)
Step 33. Purchase spring-blooming bulbs like tulips and daffodils (1 hour)
Step 34. Check the outdoor faucets for leaks (15 minutes)
Step 35. Disinfect the pruning saws with isopropyl alcohol (15 minutes)
Step 36. Inspect the garden for invasive weeds (2 hours)
Step 37. Clean out the birdhouses and nesting boxes (45 minutes)
Step 38. Buy frost blankets for the cold frames (30 minutes)
Step 39. Place the tubers in a cardboard box (10 minutes)
Step 40. Scrub the large ceramic planters (50 minutes)
Step 41. Pack the seed packets into an airtight container (30 minutes)
Step 42. Check the condition of the wheelbarrow tires (10 minutes)
Step 43. Sift the garden soil to remove large rocks (2 hours)
Step 44. Spread wood chips over the garden paths (4 hours)
Step 45. Clean out the gutters of the garden shed (1 hour)
Step 46. Change the oil in the leaf blower (30 minutes)
Step 47. Pull up the dead tomato and pepper plants (1 hour)
Step 48. Cure the tubers in a cool, dry place (1 week)
Step 49. Apply a coat of wax to the snow shovel blade (15 minutes)
Step 50. Move the heavy planters into the garage (1 hour)
Step 51. Chop the dead vegetable plants for the compost bin (1 hour)
Step 52. Pull the last of the summer weeds (3 hours)
Step 53. Shut off the main water valve to the garden (10 minutes)
Step 54. Spread a layer of mulch over the bulb beds (2 hours)
Step 55. Install the frost blankets over sensitive herbs (40 minutes)
Step 56. Cut back the withered hostas (45 minutes)
Step 57. Set up the windbreak screens (1.5 hours)
Step 58. Pack the tubers in peat moss for long-term storage (1 hour)
Step 59. Prune the deadwood from the oak trees (3 hours)
Step 60. Check the inventory of rock salt and sand (20 minutes)
Step 61. Wrap the boxwood shrubs in burlap (2 hours)
Step 62. Inspect the garden fence for holes (1 hour)
Step 63. Cover the garden beds with a heavy tarp (30 minutes)
Step 64. Drain the birdbath and cover it (20 minutes)
Step 65. Tie up the tall ornamental grasses (30 minutes)
Step 66. Inspect the irrigation timer batteries (5 minutes)
Step 67. Brush off the dirt from the garden gloves (10 minutes)
Step 68. Sharpen the lawnmower blade (30 minutes)
Step 69. Scatter wildflower seeds for spring germination (1 hour)
Step 70. Wash the garden work boots (20 minutes)
Step 71. Clean the debris out of the cold frame (30 minutes)
Step 72. Place heavy stones on the tarp edges (20 minutes)
Step 73. Check the weather forecast for the first hard freeze (10 minutes)
Step 74. Organize the winter salt spreaders (30 minutes)
Step 75. Move the bird feeders to their winter locations (30 minutes)
Step 76. Apply a final treatment of lawn fertilizer (1 hour)
Step 77. Power wash the patio stones (2 hours)
Step 78. Buy a new pair of heavy-duty garden gloves (30 minutes)
Step 79. Oil the pivot points on the loppers (10 minutes)
Step 80. Clear the leaves from the drainage grates (45 minutes)
Step 81. Sort through the garden labels and markers (30 minutes)
Step 82. Store the patio furniture cushions (20 minutes)
Step 83. Cut back the lavender plants (40 minutes)
Step 84. Inspect the trellis for stability (30 minutes)
Step 85. Move the rain barrels inside (1 hour)
Step 86. Rake the remaining lawn thatch (2 hours)
Step 87. Sort the summer bulbs for storage (1 hour)
Step 88. Clean the garden work bench (30 minutes)
Step 89. Check the snow blower spark plug (15 minutes)
Step 90. Scrub the bird feeder trays (30 minutes)
Step 91. Weigh down the mulch with light branches (1 hour)
Step 92. Shred the remaining yard waste (2 hours)
Step 93. Sanitize the garden trowels (20 minutes)
Step 94. Check the condition of the garden gate hinges (10 minutes)
Step 95. Store the watering cans upside down (10 minutes)
Step 96. Map out the planting plan for next spring (2 hours)
Step 97. Apply anti-desiccant spray to broadleaf evergreens (1 hour)
Step 98. Take a final inventory of garden chemicals (30 minutes)
Step 99. Spread a thin layer of lime on the lawn (1 hour)
Step 100. Dispose of any diseased plant material (45 minutes)
